title: NAVIGATION AND COMMUNICATION S-BAND PHASED ARRAY - EXPRO PLUS
description: In 2022, the Mars Communication and Navigation Infrastructure (MARCONI) mission concept wasstudied in the Concurrent Design Facility (CDF). The need for dual-polarized Rx/Tx S-band antennaproviding communication and navigation services has been identified. Thismultibeam antenna willneed to provide two services simultaneously:- Tx/RX Communication Service: working in S-band (2025-2300 MHz) in Left Hand CircularPolarization, the antenna shall provide the capability to receive and transmit data from Marslander and orbital assets. High directional beams with >22dBi gain within FoV (EoC=+-21deg)are required based on preliminary link budget. A trade-off (mass, volume, power, networkcomplexity, etc.) is needed to choose between a reconfigurable or a fixed multi-beam antenna(total number of beams to be defined during the activity). A simplified antenna model (notreconfigurable) shall be designed and manufactured for the proof of concept (using as much aspossible COTS components).- Navigation Service : working in S-Band (2483.5 - 2500 MHz) in Right Hand Circular Polarization,the antenna shall broadcast a navigation signal to all the assets available in the FoV (21deghalf cone TBC) generating a pattern able to provide a constant power flux density on groundover the full FoV in the Mars surface (an isoflux like pattern should be considered during thestudy).The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidate the antenna requirements and conduct a trade-off of different antennaarchitectures- Design the selected simplified antenna architecture- Manufacture a representative breadboard- Test and validate the antenna breadboard RF performance

title: Hall-Effect Thruster
description: The subject of this procurement is a Hall-effect thruster system for small satellites with <150 kg mass. The thruster will be used for performance and verification testing on engineering model level for future small satellite missions. The objectives are to understand thruster characteristics (thrust measurement, continuous operation), gain practical experience with the propulsion system, and to derive integration requirements for a small satellite mission (thruster operation, thermal soak-back, electromagnetic compatibility, cathode lifetime etc.) for Fraunhofer EMI?s next spacecraft missions. There is currently no specific mission design but different mission options, for which an application of the truster is intended as part of a dedicated propulsion system. Hall-Effect Thruster
